In [[mathematics]], '''Fontaine's period rings''' are a collection of [[commutative ring]]s first defined by [[Jean-Marc Fontaine]]<ref>Fontaine (1982)</ref> that are used to classify <math>p</math>-adic [[Galois representation]]s.

==The ring B<sub>dR</sub>==
The ring <math>\mathbf{B}_{dR}</math> is defined as follows. Let <math>\C_p</math> denote the completion of <math>\overline{\Q_p}</math>. Let

:<math>\tilde{\mathbf{E}}^+ = \varprojlim_{x\mapsto x^p} \mathcal{O}_{\C_p}/(p).</math>

An element of <math>\tilde{\mathbf{E}}^+</math> is a sequence <math>(x_1,x_2,\ldots)</math> of elements 
<math>x_i\in \mathcal{O}_{\C_p}/(p)</math> such that <math>x_{i+1}^p \equiv x_i \!\!\!\pmod p</math>. There is a natural projection map <math>f:\tilde{\mathbf{E}}^+ \to \mathcal{O}_{\C_p}/(p)</math> given by <math>f(x_1,x_2,\dotsc) = x_1</math>. There is also a multiplicative (but not additive) map <math>t:\tilde{\mathbf{E}}^+\to \mathcal{O}_{\C_p}</math> defined by
:<math>t(x_1,x_2,\dotsc) = \lim_{i\to \infty} \tilde x_i^{p^i}</math>, 
where the <math>\tilde x_i</math> are arbitrary lifts of the <math>x_i</math> to <math>\mathcal{O}_{\C_p}</math>. The composite of <math>t</math> with the projection <math>\mathcal{O}_{\C_p}\to \mathcal{O}_{\C_p}/(p)</math> is just <math>f</math>. 

The general theory of [[Witt vectors]]  yields a unique [[ring homomorphism]] <math>\theta:W(\tilde{\mathbf{E}}^+) \to \mathcal{O}_{\C_p}</math> such that <math>\theta([x]) = t(x)</math> for all <math>x\in \tilde{\mathbf{E}}^+</math>, where <math>[x]</math> denotes the [[Teichmüller representative]] of <math>x</math>. The ring <math>\mathbf{B}_{dR}^+</math> is defined to be completion of <math>\tilde{\mathbf{B}}^+ = W(\tilde{\mathbf{E}}^+)[1/p]</math> with respect to the ideal <math>\ker( \theta : \tilde{\mathbf{B}}^+ \to \C_p)</math>. Finally, the field <math>\mathbf{B}_{dR}</math> is just the [[field of fractions]] of <math>\mathbf{B}_{dR}^+</math>.
